objectives: Survey tensions: H_0, S_8, neutrino mass.

slides.title: Tensions: H_0, S_8, neutrino mass + dynamical dark energy
slides.body:
**ΛCDM tensions**: discrepancies between independent probes that may herald new physics, or hidden systematics.

**1. Hubble tension (H_0)**: persistent ~5σ disagreement.

- **Early-universe (CMB-anchored)**: Planck 2018 base-ΛCDM gives **H_0 = 67.36 ± 0.54 km/s/Mpc**. Inferred from sound horizon + angular distance to LSS. Consistent with ACT + SPT.
- **Late-universe (distance-ladder)**: SH0ES (Riess et al. 2022 ApJL): Cepheids in SN Ia host galaxies calibrate Type Ia SNe → **H_0 = 73.04 ± 1.04 km/s/Mpc**. 5.0σ tension with Planck.
- **Other late-universe**:
  - **TRGB (tip of red giant branch)**: Freedman et al. (CCHP) → 69.8 ± 1.7 (intermediate).
  - **Mira variables**: Huang et al. → 73 ± 2.
  - **JWST recalibration** (Riess 2024 + Freedman 2024): JWST imaging removes some Cepheid blending; H_0 stays ~73 with slightly enlarged errors.
  - **Strong lensing time delays (H0LiCOW + TDCOSMO)**: 73.3 ± 1.7 (late) — later analyses with priors → wider range.
  - **Standard sirens (GW170817)**: 70 ± 7 (consistent with both).
- **Inverse distance ladder** (BAO + BBN + SNe; no CMB): 67-68 (close to Planck).
- **eBOSS BAO + BBN**: 67-68 (Planck-consistent).

**Possible resolutions**:
- **Systematics**: Cepheid metallicity, extinction, Mira population II/I — historically have resolved tensions but current systematics tightly constrained.
- **Early dark energy (EDE)** (Karwal-Kamionkowski 2016; Smith + Poulin 2019): pre-recombination component (~10% of Ω_r before equality) reduces sound horizon → H_0 inferred from CMB shifts up. Tension with S_8 + LSS, partially.
- **Acoustic dark energy / NEDE / SIDR**: variants.
- **N_eff > 3.046** (extra light relics): SU(N) hidden sectors, sterile ν.
- **Decaying dark matter**: DM → radiation post-recombination → H_0 shift.
- **Modified gravity / late-time dark energy**: w(z) ≠ -1.
- **Local underdensity**: 'Hubble bubble' — disfavored by SN samples.
- **New physics at recombination**: modified recombination history.

**Status**: most natural single-fix models partially address H_0 at cost of worsening S_8 or N_eff fits. No 'silver bullet' resolution.

**2. S_8 / σ_8 tension**: ~2-3σ discrepancy in matter clustering amplitude.

- **S_8 ≡ σ_8 · √(Ω_m/0.3)**.
- **Planck (CMB)**: S_8 = 0.832 ± 0.013.
- **Weak lensing** (KiDS-1000, DES Y3, HSC Y3): S_8 ≈ 0.76-0.78 ± 0.02; ~2-3σ low.
- **Cluster counts** (Planck-SZ, eROSITA): also slightly low.
- **Lyman-α + RSD**: mixed but generally consistent with Planck or slightly lower.

**Possible resolutions**:
- **Suppressed nonlinear power**: massive neutrinos (Σm_ν ~ 0.1 eV), warm DM, baryonic feedback (AGN ejecting hot gas).
- **Systematics in shear measurement** (multiplicative bias, photo-z, intrinsic alignments).
- **EDE worsens S_8**: tension with H_0 fix.
- **Modified gravity** (f(R), DGP): suppresses growth.

**3. Neutrino mass Σm_ν**:
- **Cosmology** (CMB + LSS): Σm_ν < 0.12 eV (Planck + BAO; 95% CL).
- **Oscillation experiments** (Super-K, T2K, NOvA, IceCube, JUNO): require Σm_ν ≥ 0.06 eV (normal hierarchy) or ≥ 0.10 eV (inverted).
- **Cosmological + oscillation overlap**: cosmology now excludes inverted hierarchy at ~2σ (if no new physics).
- **Future**: DESI + Euclid + CMB-S4 + LiteBIRD will reach σ(Σm_ν) ~ 20 meV — decisive.

**4. Other anomalies**:
- **CMB low-ℓ anomalies**: cold spot, low quadrupole, axis-of-evil; ~2σ tensions; mostly statistical.
- **Hemispherical power asymmetry**: detected in WMAP + Planck; ~3σ.
- **DESI 2024 dynamical w hint**: w₀ ≈ -0.55, w_a ≈ -1.4; 2.5-3.9σ deviation from Λ.
- **JWST high-z galaxy abundance**: more massive z > 10 galaxies than predicted; possible early stellar formation efficiency.
- **Lithium problem**: BBN predicts ⁷Li ~3× observed; persistent.
- **CMB-S4 + LiteBIRD r ~ 10⁻³**: not detected → constrain inflation models.

slides.title: New observational windows: 21cm, GWs, JWST, Euclid, LSST
slides.body:
**Cosmology is entering a multi-messenger + multi-window era**: 21cm radio, gravitational waves, neutrinos, high-z galaxies, weak lensing, CMB polarization — all converging on percent-level precision.

**21-cm cosmology**: neutral hydrogen hyperfine transition (1420 MHz rest; redshifted to ~50-500 MHz for z = 2-30). Probes dark ages + cosmic dawn + reionization where no luminous sources exist.

- **EDGES 2018** (Bowman + Rogers, MIT Haystack): claimed absorption feature at 78 MHz (z ≈ 17, cosmic dawn) with anomalous depth — possibly DM-baryon interactions. Contested; SARAS-3 + REACH + MIST + LEDA do not confirm; foreground/calibration issues. Hidden source of excitement.
- **HERA** (Hydrogen Epoch of Reionization Array, South Africa, 2017-): targeting 21cm power spectrum at z = 6-10. Constraints on heating + reionization history.
- **LOFAR** (Netherlands array): cosmic dawn imaging attempts.
- **MWA** (Murchison Widefield Array, Australia): power spectrum.
- **SKA** (Square Kilometre Array, South Africa + Australia; SKA-Low 2028+, SKA-Mid 2028+): full power spectrum + tomographic imaging from z=1 to z=30; cosmic dawn revolution.
- **CHIME / HIRAX / CHORD**: intensity mapping at z = 0.8-2.5 (BAO + DE).

**Gravitational waves**: a new spectrum from 10⁻¹⁸ Hz (CMB B-modes) to kHz (LIGO).

- **LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA O5 (2025-2027)**: ~100s of BBH mergers/yr + several NS mergers + perhaps NSBH; population statistics + multi-messenger.
- **LISA** (Laser Interferometer Space Antenna, ESA + NASA, ~2035 launch): mHz band; supermassive BH mergers (10⁵-10⁷ M⊙) + EMRIs (extreme mass-ratio inspirals) + galactic binaries; stochastic GW background from early universe.
- **Einstein Telescope (ET)** + **Cosmic Explorer (CE)** (~2035+): 3rd-generation ground; ~10× LIGO sensitivity.
- **NANOGrav 2023** (15-year data release): nHz stochastic background detection at ~3σ; supermassive BH binaries + primordial origins possible. Pulsar timing arrays (PTA) — also EPTA, PPTA, CPTA; SKA will dominate.
- **Standard sirens**: GW170817 H_0 = 70 ± 7; many more from O5 + LISA.
- **Primordial GW background (B-modes)**: SO (r < 0.003), CMB-S4 (r < 10⁻³), LiteBIRD; targets r ~ 10⁻³.

**JWST 2022+** (NASA + ESA + CSA Webb telescope, L2): IR observations 0.6-28 μm.
- **Cosmic dawn galaxies**: z > 10 galaxies more massive + abundant than ΛCDM-base-feedback predicts; 'JWST excess'. Could be: early star formation efficiency, top-heavy IMF, primordial BHs.
- **Reionization sources**: galaxy LyC escape fraction, ionizing photon budget.
- **Cepheid recalibration**: Riess 2024 + Freedman 2024 refine SH0ES H_0 = 73 with JWST imaging.
- **High-z quasars**: SMBH formation channels.
- **JADES, CEERS, COSMOS-Web, UNCOVER, PRIMER**: deep + wide surveys.

**Euclid 2023+** (ESA, 1.2m telescope L2; launched 1 Jul 2023):
- 14000 deg² survey to 24 mag (visible) + 24 mag (NIR).
- ~1.5×10⁹ galaxy shapes (weak lensing).
- ~50M spectroscopic galaxies (BAO + RSD).
- Targets: w(z) precision; S_8 precision; modified gravity.
- First results expected 2025.

**Roman Space Telescope** (NASA, 2.4m, L2; 2027 launch):
- 2200 deg² high-latitude survey + microlensing + transient survey.
- ~10M deep spectroscopic + 100M photometric galaxies.
- ~5000 SN Ia to z ~ 2.
- Complements Euclid (different band) + LSST (different cadence + depth).

**Vera C. Rubin Observatory + LSST 2025+** (NSF + DOE; 8.4m Simonyi Survey Telescope, Cerro Pachón Chile):
- 18000 deg², ugrizy 24-27 mag, every 3 nights for 10 years.
- ~20B galaxies + ~5M SNe + ~17B stars (incl. milky-way halo) + asteroids.
- Survey starts Oct 2025; first major dark-energy + DM constraints by ~2030.
- Cross-correlations with CMB-S4 (matter lensing), Euclid (shape), Roman (spectra), DESI (z).

**CMB-S4 + LiteBIRD** (2030s):
- CMB-S4 (US DOE/NSF, Antarctica + Atacama, 500000 detectors): r < 10⁻³; σ_8, τ, Σm_ν percent.
- LiteBIRD (JAXA, 2032 launch): full-sky polarization at low-ℓ; complements CMB-S4 small-scale.

**Neutrino telescopes**:
- **IceCube-Gen2**: 8× IceCube; high-energy astrophysical neutrinos; ν cosmology.
- **KM3NeT**: Mediterranean ν telescope.
- **DUNE**: long-baseline ν oscillations; Σm_ν, hierarchy.

**Dark-matter direct + indirect detection**:
- **LZ → DARWIN/XLZD** (~50-tonne Xe TPC, ~2030): WIMP cross-section ~10⁻⁴⁹ cm² (ν floor).
- **ADMX-EFR + DMRadio + ABRACADABRA**: axion mass range expansion.
- **CTA (Cherenkov Telescope Array)**: γ-ray indirect detection; ν-DM annihilation.

**Combined power**: the 2025-2035 decade will be among the most data-rich in cosmology's history. ΛCDM will be tested at sub-percent precision; tensions will be resolved or confirmed; possible new physics (EDE, dynamical w, light relics, modified gravity, DM particle nature) within reach.

slides.title: AI for cosmology: SBI, emulators, N-body surrogates, LLMs
slides.body:
**AI + ML for cosmology** has exploded since ~2018, accelerating analysis + simulation pipelines + enabling problem classes intractable before.

**1. Emulators**: replace expensive cosmological calculations with fast NN surrogates.
- **CMB power spectrum emulators** (CosmoNet, CMBPyrEmu, NUMICO): replace CAMB/CLASS Boltzmann code (~sec/call) with NN (~ms/call) — 100-1000× speedup. Used in MCMC parameter inference (Planck, ACT, CMB-S4 forecasts).
- **N-body emulators** (CosmicEmu, EuclidEmulator, BACCOemu, FORGE): predict nonlinear matter power spectrum P(k, z, cosmo) from sparse training simulations (CAMELS, ABACUSSummit, Quijote). Emulate to sub-percent accuracy over k < 5 h/Mpc.
- **Cluster mass emulators** (Mira-Titan, Aemulus): halo mass functions, concentration-mass relations.
- **NVIDIA + collaborations**: physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for cosmological N-body. **Lemos et al. 2024** showed transformer-based N-body emulators reproducing 1024³ simulations in seconds.

**2. Simulation-based inference (SBI)**: forward-model cosmology → marginalize over nuisance via NN density estimators.
- **Likelihood-free / approximate Bayesian computation (ABC)**: replace analytic likelihood with sampled simulations.
- **Neural density estimators**: normalizing flows (MAF, NSF) + neural ratio estimation (NRE).
- **SBI** for cluster cosmology (Hahn + Villaescusa-Navarro 2023): joint LSS + photometric + spectroscopic.
- **SimBIG (Hahn 2024)**: SBI for SDSS-BOSS galaxy clustering → tightened constraints.
- Advantages: handles complex non-Gaussian summary statistics (e.g., field-level inference, persistent homology, scattering transforms).
- Drawbacks: requires huge simulation suites (CAMELS, FastPM, Quijote).

**3. N-body surrogates**:
- **Pylians + nbodykit**: cosmology + structure formation Python toolkits.
- **Lemos et al. 2023**: ML surrogates that replace 1024³ N-body in seconds — enables Bayesian inference over millions of cosmologies.
- **NVIDIA Modulus + JAX-Cosmo**: GPU-accelerated differentiable simulators.
- **CAMELS-SAM**: subset of CAMELS for stellar halo modeling.

**4. ML for analyses**:
- **Field-level inference**: instead of compressing data to power spectrum, train NNs on entire density fields. Captures non-Gaussianity, higher-order moments.
- **Cosmological parameter inference from images**: CNNs on weak-lensing convergence maps (Fluri et al. 2018, Ribli et al. 2019); ~2× tighter constraints than power spectrum.
- **Foregrounds in CMB + 21cm**: ML separation of dust + synchrotron from cosmological signal.
- **Galaxy + cluster classification**: morphology, photometric redshifts, deblending.
- **SN Ia + transient classification**: PLAsTiCC, RESSPECT; LSST will produce ~10M transient alerts/night.
- **Cosmological N-body emulators for DESI + LSST**: AbacusSummit-trained emulators are accurate to sub-percent.

**5. LLMs + foundation models for theory + literature**:
- **AstroBERT, Astro-LLaMA**: domain-adapted models for arXiv astro-ph search + summarization.
- **arxivGPT, Galactica, BLOOM-astro**: cosmology-tuned generative models.
- **Anthropic Claude + OpenAI GPT-4/5 + Gemini**: general LLMs for literature review, code generation (CAMB scripts, mock pipelines), proofreading. Increasingly used by working cosmologists.
- **Specialized agents**: hypothesis generation, paper summarization, code assistance.
- **Mathematical reasoning**: in numerical + symbolic computation — Mathematica/Sage integration.

**6. Specific exciting ML cosmology lines (2022-2025)**:
- **Birrer + lens modeling**: ML accelerated strong-gravitational-lens modeling for H_0 from time delays.
- **Field-level inference with simulation-based inference**: full-resolution cosmology from LSS images.
- **CMB delensing with ML**: removes lensing-induced B-modes to recover primordial GWs.
- **GW signal reconstruction**: PyCBC + Bilby + ML denoising.
- **Dark-matter substructure**: ML on strong lensing arcs to find DM substructure (Vegetti 2010, Brehmer + Cranmer 2018 + 2019, Adam + Hezaveh 2022).
- **N-body initial-conditions reconstruction**: machine-learned displacement fields.
- **JWST high-z galaxy modeling**: feedback emulators + parameter inference.

**7. Challenges + open problems**:
- **Training data**: even with CAMELS (4000 sims) + ABACUSSummit (~150 sims), parameter coverage is limited.
- **Out-of-distribution generalization**: emulators may fail for parameters far from training grid.
- **Interpretability**: ML 'black-box' inferences raise concerns about systematics + posterior calibration.
- **Cross-validation across pipelines**: independent groups need to validate ML predictions vs traditional analyses.

**The future**: by 2030, ML pipelines will likely dominate cosmological analysis — from N-body emulation through field-level inference through LLM-augmented theory. Survey scale (LSST alone: ~10 PB/yr) makes traditional analysis intractable. The cosmologist's role becomes architecting + validating ML pipelines + interpreting their physical meaning.

**'Cosmology in the AI era'**: faster, more flexible, increasingly automated — but the foundational physics (FLRW, GR, inflation, ΛCDM) + observational measurements (CMB, LSS, BAO, SNe) remain the scientific bedrock. AI accelerates the pipeline; the physics drives the questions.

question.question: Quantify the Hubble tension significance
question.goal: Given Planck H_0 = 67.4 ± 0.5 + SH0ES H_0 = 73.0 ± 1.0, compute the tension significance in standard deviations.

steps.reveal: Tension = ΔH/σ ≈ 5.6/1.12 ≈ 5.0σ. Far above the 3σ threshold often used to declare 'significant' tension; corresponds to ~5×10⁻⁷ p-value if statistical. Persistent for ~7 years now (since Riess 2016).

steps.prompt: Why is the 5σ tension hard to dismiss?

acceptedAnswers: Replicated by multiple independent teams + multiple distance indicators (Cepheids, TRGB, Mira, lensing); not single-experiment outlier

steps.reveal: Replicated by independent teams (SH0ES Cepheids ~73; H0LiCOW lensing ~73; Mira ~73; intermediate TRGB ~70). CMB-anchored estimates consistent across Planck, ACT, SPT, WMAP, BAO+BBN. JWST recalibration confirms ~73 (Riess + Freedman 2024). Hard to dismiss as single-experiment error. Possible: (a) Cepheid systematic (metallicity, extinction); (b) early-universe new physics shifting r_s; (c) late-time DE evolution; (d) statistical fluctuation (now < 10⁻⁶).

acceptedAnswers: Independent H_0: GW standard sirens (LISA), gravitational lensing time delays, Type II SNe; or new physics confirmed by CMB-S4/LiteBIRD/DESI; or systematic discovery in distance ladder

steps.reveal: Independent H_0 measurements: (i) standard sirens from LIGO O5 + LISA (NS-NS + BBH); (ii) strong-lens time delays from H0LiCOW + TDCOSMO + JWST; (iii) Type II SNe (Standardized Candles in the Forest); (iv) cosmic chronometers (massive passively evolving galaxies). New physics: detection of EDE signature in CMB-S4 polarization; r-detection narrows inflation models; light-relic detection N_eff. By 2030, likely either: (a) systematics-driven resolution; (b) confirmed new pre-recombination physics. Either outcome major science.

question.question: Why are simulation-based inference (SBI) + N-body emulators (Lemos, NVIDIA) revolutionizing cosmological analysis?
options: Traditional cosmological analysis: compress data (CMB, galaxy P(k), weak-lensing shear) to summary statistics (power spectrum, BAO position) + compute analytic Gaussian likelihood. Limits: (i) compressing throws away non-Gaussian information; (ii) analytic likelihoods invalid at nonlinear scales; (iii) systematic modeling requires marginalization. **Simulation-based inference (SBI)**: forward-model the entire data-generation process via simulations, then use NN density estimators (normalizing flows, neural ratio estimation) to infer posterior on cosmological parameters — bypassing analytic likelihood. **N-body emulators** (CosmicEmu, BACCOemu, NVIDIA Lemos transformer-based 2024): replace ~10⁶ CPU-hour N-body sims with NN surrogates that run in seconds → enables Bayesian inference over thousands of cosmologies. **Field-level inference** retains full image-level information (CNN on weak-lensing convergence maps) → ~2× tighter constraints than power spectrum. Used for: SimBIG (SDSS-BOSS), DESI mock pipelines, Euclid, Roman, LSST cosmology forecasts. ML now dominates next-generation cosmology pipelines.
question.explanation: SBI + N-body emulators enable Bayesian inference at nonlinear scales + with non-Gaussian summary statistics. Emulators (CosmicEmu, BACCO, NVIDIA Lemos 2024 transformer) replace ~10⁶ CPU-hour N-body sims with ms-scale NN evaluations. Field-level inference retains full image-level info → ~2× tighter constraints. SimBIG, DESI, Euclid, Roman, LSST forecasts use SBI + emulators. Will dominate next-gen cosmology.

slides.workedSolution: Traditional Gaussian-likelihood analysis throws away non-Gaussian info + fails at nonlinear scales. SBI forward-models entire data pipeline via simulations + uses normalizing flows / NRE to infer posterior. N-body emulators (Lemos, NVIDIA) replace 10⁶ CPU-hr sims with NN surrogates running in seconds → Bayesian inference across thousands of cosmologies feasible. Field-level inference retains all spatial info → tighter constraints. Now dominant in DESI, Euclid, Roman, LSST pipelines.

question.question: By 2030, CMB-S4 + DESI-II + Euclid + Roman jointly find: H_0 = 70.5 ± 0.3, w_0 = -0.95 ± 0.02, w_a = -0.2 ± 0.05, Σm_ν = 0.08 ± 0.01 eV.
question.prompt: What do these imply for: H_0 tension (resolved?), dynamical dark energy (yes/no?), neutrino hierarchy (normal vs inverted?), modified gravity, + ΛCDM as standard model? Discuss how this constrains: EDE, decaying DM, neutrino-cosmology link, swampland conjectures. What follow-up would discriminate Λ from quintessence + phantom?

question.question: Write the S_8 clustering amplitude parameter (used in weak-lensing analyses).
question.hint: Combines amplitude σ_8 with matter density Ω_m, normalized at 0.3 reference value.

question.prompt: In ≤120 words, summarize the next decade's frontier in cosmology + the role of AI.
question.rubric: Mentions: 2025-2035 cosmology decade dominated by major facilities — Vera Rubin LSST (2025+, 20B galaxies + 5M SNe), Euclid (2023+ launched, 1.5B shapes + 50M spectra), Roman (2027+ launch, deep IR + SNe), DESI (2021-2026 BAO + RSD), CMB-S4 (~2030 r ~ 10⁻³), LiteBIRD (2032 launch full-sky polarization), SKA (2028+ 21cm), LISA (~2035 mHz GWs), DARWIN/XLZD (~2030 DM direct), ADMX-EFR (axions), CTA (γ-ray DM). Tensions resolved or confirmed: H_0 (5σ; new physics or systematics?), S_8 (~3σ), neutrino mass (Σm_ν 60-120 meV?), DESI 2024 w₀w_a hint. AI revolution: SBI + N-body emulators (Lemos NVIDIA transformer), field-level inference, ML foregrounds, LLMs for theory + literature. Faster pipelines, more flexible, capturing non-Gaussian info. ΛCDM tested at sub-percent across multiple probes; possible new physics within reach. Cosmology + AI converge into the most data-driven era yet.
